day_16.decision: Proceed to Day 17 with KNN Hamming matching, ratio filtering, cross-check comparison, match-distance diagnostics, and match spatial-coverage diagnostics.
interpretation: ORB feature availability changes with image content and appearance or geometric modification, so later matching quality should be interpreted together with keypoint count and spatial coverage.
A large keypoint count alone is not evidence that a reliable transform can be estimated. Day 17 must test descriptor correspondence quality before any geometric conclusion is made.
limitations: Day 16 measures detection and descriptor extraction only. It does not measure keypoint repeatability, correspondence correctness, or registration accuracy because descriptor matching has not been introduced yet.
The observations are specific to the tracked images, configured transformations, OpenCV ORB settings, and the machine used for this run.
observations: The largest moving-image keypoint count occurred in camera_identity with 800 keypoints.
The smallest moving-image keypoint count occurred in moon_blur with 36 keypoints.
The strongest keypoint-count reduction relative to its fixed image occurred in moon_blur, with a moving-to-fixed count ratio of 0.062.
The lowest 4x4 spatial coverage occurred in moon_blur at 0.375.

The configured n_features cap of 800 was reached in camera_identity, camera_translation, camera_rotation, camera_scale, camera_illumination. Counts in those cases are capped and should not be interpreted as the total number of detectable features.
All configured Day 16 cases produced ORB descriptors in both images.
day_16.title: ORB keypoint detection and binary descriptor extraction

validation.note: The captured pytest console output did not include the final numeric test-count summary, so the findings registry records the successful exit code rather than inferring a pass count.
validation.target_windows_experiment: 8 / 8 configured cases produced descriptors in both images

day_17.decision: Use the Day 17 correspondences as input to Day 18 RANSAC similarity estimation, where geometric inliers and outliers can be measured explicitly.
interpretation: The ratio threshold controls a trade-off between retaining more correspondences and accepting more ambiguous descriptor matches.
Accepted-match count and spatial coverage should be interpreted together. Many matches concentrated in a small region may still provide weak geometric support.
Cross-check and ratio filtering apply different correspondence rules, so their match counts should not be interpreted as direct quality scores without geometric validation.
limitations: Day 17 evaluates descriptor correspondence filtering only. No RANSAC model is fitted and no registration transform is estimated.
A descriptor match can pass the current filter and still be geometrically incorrect.
The development findings are specific to the tracked images, ORB settings, matching thresholds, and selected controlled conditions.
observations: At the default ratio threshold, camera_identity produced the largest accepted KNN match count with 800 matches.
At the default ratio threshold, moon_blur produced the smallest accepted KNN match count with 29 matches.
The lowest accepted-correspondence grid coverage occurred in moon_blur with minimum fixed/moving coverage 0.375.
Across the configured cases, relaxing the ratio threshold from 0.60 to 0.90 changed the mean accepted-match count from 404.2 to 556.7.
day_17.title: ORB descriptor matching and correspondence filtering

validation.environment: Windows PowerShell project virtual environment, Python 3.12.6
validation.target_windows_experiment: 9 / 9 configured cases retained at least 8 matches for both KNN ratio filtering and cross-check matching

day_18.decision: Proceed to Day 19 with affine RANSAC, degeneracy checks, texture stratification, and threshold sweeps while retaining the Day 18 similarity baseline.
interpretation: RANSAC adds a geometric consistency test after descriptor filtering. Accepted ORB matches are not automatically treated as correct correspondences.
Inlier ratio, reprojection residuals, and ground-truth TRE describe different parts of the result and should be reported together.
A successful RANSAC call is not sufficient evidence of correct registration. Geometric correctness is evaluated separately against the known transform.
limitations: Day 18 evaluates only the similarity model. General affine estimation and degeneracy checks are reserved for Day 19.
The current development thresholds are working thresholds for controlled experiments and are not final benchmark thresholds.
The findings are specific to the tracked images, ORB configuration, ratio filter, RANSAC settings, and selected controlled transformations.
observations: The smallest geometric error occurred in camera_similarity_illumination with TRE 0.110 px.
The largest geometric error occurred in camera_similarity_large with TRE 0.556 px.
The lowest RANSAC inlier ratio occurred in camera_similarity_blur at 0.788.
The controlled outlier experiment injected 126 incorrect correspondences; RANSAC rejected 126 of those injected correspondences.
day_18.title: ORB + RANSAC similarity estimation and outlier rejection

validation.environment: Windows PowerShell project virtual environment, Python 3.12.6
validation.target_windows_experiment: 8 / 8 RANSAC estimates succeeded and 8 / 8 were within the configured Day 18 development tolerances

day_19.decision: Carry the validated affine model, explicit failure rules, texture diagnostics, and threshold-sweep evidence into the Day 20 integrated feature-based benchmark.
interpretation: The affine model can represent anisotropic scale and shear that a similarity model cannot, but the additional freedom requires stronger geometric guardrails.
Feature count alone is not sufficient for reliable affine estimation. Spatial coverage, collinearity, RANSAC inlier consistency, and transform plausibility are recorded separately.
Ratio filtering and RANSAC reprojection thresholds interact. A threshold that retains more correspondences is not automatically the setting with the lowest geometric error.
Texture diagnostics are descriptive stratification variables. They help explain feature availability but do not by themselves determine registration success.
limitations: The Day 19 thresholds are development settings and are not frozen final benchmark settings.
Texture labels use configured gradient-energy thresholds and a capped ORB detector, so the categories are specific to this experiment setup.
The procedural repeated-pattern case is a controlled ambiguity probe and is not a substitute for diverse real repeated structures.
Similarity and affine model comparisons are limited to the shared Day 19 cases and should not be generalized beyond the current benchmark.
observations: The smallest affine TRE occurred in camera_affine_mild at 0.111 px.
The largest returned affine TRE occurred in low_texture_affine at 15.599 px, and that estimate was rejected for insufficient RANSAC inliers.
The lowest successful-case affine RANSAC inlier ratio occurred in coins_affine at 0.802. The rejected low_texture_affine case had an inlier ratio of 0.750.

Affine RANSAC produced lower TRE than similarity RANSAC on all seven true-affine cases where both models returned a numeric TRE. The repeated-pattern case produced no filtered matches, so no model comparison was possible there.
The three controlled degeneracy and plausibility probes produced their expected failure labels in 3 of 3 probes.
The threshold sweep produced 80 within-tolerance results across 120 case and threshold combinations.
day_19.title: Affine RANSAC, degeneracy checks, texture diagnostics, and threshold sweeps

validation.environment: Windows PowerShell project virtual environment, Python 3.12.6
validation.target_windows_experiment: 7 / 9 affine RANSAC cases succeeded and 7 / 9 were within the configured Day 19 development tolerances

day_20.decision: Close Week 4 and carry the shared-case comparison policy, explicit feature failure records, and integrated result schema into the multimodal mutual-information stage.
interpretation: The integrated benchmark keeps comparison groups separate so methods are compared only on shared cases with compatible geometric intent.
Translation, rigid, and affine results are not combined into one universal ranking because the supported motion models and model flexibility differ.
Feature matching success, RANSAC estimation success, and ground-truth geometric success remain separate recorded states.
The low-texture and repeated-pattern cases are diagnostic failure probes and are reported separately from the shared comparison groups.
limitations: The current thresholds are development thresholds and are not frozen final benchmark criteria.
The integrated comparison uses a compact controlled subset and does not establish general method superiority.

ORB similarity has one scale degree of freedom beyond ECC rigid on the rigid comparison group, so that comparison is a shared-case behavior comparison rather than an equal-complexity model comparison.
The current comparison remains monomodal. Real and simulated multimodal method comparison is reserved for the mutual-information stage.

day_20.title: Integrated feature-based benchmark and shared-case comparison

sift_stage_01.decision: Carry ratio threshold 0.75 provisionally into SIFT Stage 2, where similarity and affine RANSAC will determine whether the retained correspondences are geometrically consistent.
interpretation: SIFT uses 128-dimensional floating-point descriptors and L2 distance, so its descriptor distances are not directly comparable with ORB Hamming distances.
Accepted-match count and spatial coverage are descriptive inputs to later geometric estimation. They are not registration-accuracy metrics.
The ratio threshold remains provisional because Stage 1 does not test geometric inliers or ground-truth registration error.
limitations: Stage 1 evaluates SIFT detection, description, and correspondence filtering only. No RANSAC transform is estimated.
The subset is intentionally small and uses tracked monomodal images with controlled transformations and degradations.
Runtime measurements are machine-dependent and the stored runtime values refer to the validated target Windows run.
observations: moon_blur produced the fewest accepted SIFT matches at the provisional threshold with 11 matches.
camera_identity produced the most accepted SIFT matches at the provisional threshold with 791 matches.
moon_blur had the lowest accepted-correspondence spatial coverage at 0.375.
coins_rotation retained 390 accepted matches with full 4 x 4 correspondence coverage.
Relaxing the ratio threshold from 0.60 to 0.85 increased the mean accepted-match count from 341.4 to 380.7. Geometric quality will be evaluated in Stage 2.
sift_stage_01.title: SIFT detection, description, and L2 matching

validation.target_windows_experiment: 7/7 matching cases passed at ratio threshold 0.75; mean accepted matches 359.0; mean minimum spatial coverage 0.759; mean total detection runtime 79.382 ms; mean L2 matching runtime 3.425 ms.

sift_stage_02.decision: Proceed with the frozen Stage 3 ORB versus SIFT comparison without retuning the validated Stage 2 thresholds.
interpretation: Stage 2 separates SIFT descriptor filtering, RANSAC execution success, and geometric correctness against known ground truth.
The same similarity and affine RANSAC implementations used by the ORB pipeline are reused here; only the feature front-end and descriptor metric differ.
Target Windows validation confirms the Stage 2 implementation and permits the Stage 3 comparison to proceed with frozen settings.
limitations: The controlled case set is small, so observations remain case-specific.
Runtime values depend on machine, OpenCV build, and thread scheduling.
Stage 2 does not by itself determine whether SIFT should be retained in the final method set.
observations: Lowest target Windows TRE was 0.005 px for camera_partial_overlap.
Largest returned target Windows TRE was 1.247 px for low_texture_affine.
repeated_pattern_affine retained no filtered SIFT matches and failed before RANSAC.
sift_stage_02.title: SIFT + RANSAC similarity and affine registration

validation.target_windows_experiment: 12/13 matching successes; 12/13 RANSAC successes; 12/13 within configured geometric tolerances.

sift_stage_03.decision: Validate the frozen Stage 3 comparison on the target Windows environment before selecting one of the three documented SIFT retention outcomes.
interpretation: Feature count and raw match count are diagnostics, not the deciding criteria.
Registration success and geometric correctness are evaluated before difficult-case recovery, RANSAC consistency, and runtime.
A final SIFT retention decision is intentionally deferred until the same Stage 3 experiment is validated on the target Windows environment.
limitations: This tracked Stage 3 snapshot records a development-machine run until target Windows validation is supplied.
The comparison is a small controlled subset and does not establish universal superiority of either feature method.
Runtime depends on machine, OpenCV build, and thread scheduling.
observations: ORB was inside tolerance on 10 / 12 cases in this development run.
SIFT was inside tolerance on 11 / 12 cases in this development run.
Paired outcomes: 10 both passed, 0 ORB-only passes, 1 SIFT-only passes, 1 neither passed.
low_texture_affine: sift_only_within_tolerance.
repeated_pattern_affine: neither_within_tolerance.
sift_stage_03.title: Frozen ORB versus SIFT controlled comparison
